validated_work_order.understanding: The custom report's filter button can only be found by where it sits on screen. openConditionsMenu in packages/desktop-client/e2e/page-models/custom-report-page.ts:55-77 collects every button inside the reports page that has no accessible name, walks them in DOM order, takes a boundingBox() for each and clicks the first whose left edge sits right of x=850. The button it wants is CompactFiltersButton (CompactFiltersButton.tsx:6-16), which FiltersMenu.tsx:752-758 renders when the `compact` prop is set and ReportTopbar.tsx:234-235 always sets. That component renders an SvgFilter and nothing else, so the button has no accessible name today — which is exactly why the locator resorts to geometry. Two consequences: the e2e suite's conditions-menu scenarios silently skip (and then fail further down with an unrelated message) at any viewport where the topbar reflows and the button lands left of x=850, and a screen-reader user has no way to find the button at all, because an icon-only button with no name is announced as "button". Separately, the same e2e file carries two verbatim copies of selectOnlyBillsGroup (reports.test.ts:311 and :479, diffed byte-identical) and two copies of switchToAnyOf (:343 and :501, differing only by a two-line comment); both close over only `page` and `customReportPage` and both sit inside the enclosing `custom reports` describe, so one hoisted copy serves both. The sibling non-compact FiltersButton already renders the word Filter, and every other icon-only control in the same topbar (GraphButton, SnapshotButton) already sets aria-label={title} — the compact filter button is the one control in that toolbar that does not.
validated_work_order.root_cause: The compact filter button is the only icon-only control in the report topbar with no accessible name, so no role-and-name locator exists for it; the e2e page model filled the gap with a coordinate threshold (boundingBox().x > 850) that encodes the default 1280px layout rather than the control's identity.
validated_work_order.approach: Give the compact filter button the accessible name its tooltip already displays. FiltersMenu.tsx:741-747 already wraps both variants in a Tooltip whose content is `<Trans>Filters</Trans>`, so a sighted user is told "Filters" on hover while a screen-reader user is told nothing; passing the same string as aria-label makes the two agree, and gives the e2e suite a role-and-name locator that works at any viewport. The string reuses the existing `Filters` translation key — no new copy, and no locale file changes (packages/desktop-client/locale is gitignored and regenerated by yarn generate:i18n). aria-label is the right hook rather than data-testid because it is the change a person benefits from, exactly as GraphButton (GraphButton.tsx:42) and SnapshotButton (SnapshotButton.tsx:45) already do for their siblings in the same toolbar. The compact name is deliberately "Filters", matching its tooltip, while the non-compact variant's visible text is "Filter" — so `exact: true` on the name resolves to the compact button even if a non-compact one is also on the page, which is what IAC-2 asks for. Then replace the geometry scan in the page model with `this.pageContent.getByRole('button', { name: 'Filters', exact: true }).click()`: Playwright auto-waits for the locator and throws naming it when it never appears, so the failure stays loud and its message now names the control rather than a pixel threshold. Finally, hoist selectOnlyBillsGroup and switchToAnyOf out of their two nested describes into the body of the enclosing `custom reports` describe, keeping the versions that carry the fuller comments, and delete both inner copies.

qa_script: yarn start, then open http://localhost:3001 and choose "Don't use a server" -> "View demo" so the report has data.
Go to Reports, open a custom report. The topbar's rightmost control is the icon-only filter button (funnel glyph).
With the mouse elsewhere, inspect that button: it now has the accessible name 'Filters'. Hover it — the tooltip has always said 'Filters', so name and tooltip now agree.
Check the button's position in the accessibility tree / devtools: it is announced as 'Filters, button', not a bare 'button'. This is the screen-reader half of the ticket; a screenshot cannot show it.

Confirm every other topbar control still reads correctly and no layout shifted: Data Table, Bar Graph, Line Graph, Area Graph, Donut Graph, Show Legend, Show Summary, Show Labels, Download Snapshot, then the filter button and the report-name button. Nothing moved — aria-label renders nothing.
Click the filter button: the fields popover opens (Category, Account, Payee, Notes, ...). Escape out.

Narrow the window to roughly 1024px wide. The topbar reflows and the filter button moves left. It must still be clickable and must still open the same popover — this is the case that used to break the locator.

Optional, the regression suite: yarn workspace @actual-app/web run playwright test reports.test.ts --browser=chromium. Every 'custom reports' scenario must pass, including the new 'the conditions menu opens at a narrower viewport'. Say in the PR body that verify.e2e is empty in .sdlc/config.yml, so this is a local-only guard.
risks: The e2e half of this ticket has no CI guard: verify.e2e is empty in .sdlc/config.yml, so nothing the pipeline runs exercises packages/desktop-client/e2e/reports.test.ts. The new unit test (yarn test, which does run) is therefore the only regression guard CI actually executes; the e2e case is worth running locally and the PR body should say so rather than implying CI covers it.

The new narrow-viewport e2e test changes the viewport inside a mode:'serial' describe that also contains toMatchThemeScreenshots tests. If the restore in `finally` is omitted or the test throws before reaching it, later VRT snapshots are taken at 1024px and fail. The restore must be in a finally, not after the last assertion.

Adding an aria-label to a button that previously had none changes its accessible name on every surface that renders the compact variant, not only the custom report: reports/Header.tsx:185 and reports/reports/Spending.tsx:411 both pass compact={isNarrowWidth}. That is the intended improvement, but any e2e or VRT assertion that relied on those buttons being nameless would shift. Grep found no such locator — packages/desktop-client/e2e/page-models/account-page.ts:56 is the only 'Filter' name lookup and the accounts page renders the non-compact variant.

'Filters' (compact, aria-label) and 'Filter' (non-compact, visible text) are now two different accessible names for what a person experiences as the same control, differing only by width. That is intentional — it is what lets `exact: true` resolve to the compact button alone (IAC-2) — but a screen-reader user switching widths hears a slightly different word. If reviewers prefer one name everywhere, that is a deliberate follow-up, not something to smuggle in here.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add data-testid="filters-button" to CompactFiltersButton and locate by getByTestId in the page model.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The ticket asks for a hook a person benefits from and names data-testid as the fallback only when no name can be given. A name CAN be given here — the tooltip already says "Filters" and the two sibling components in the same toolbar already set aria-label — so a test id would fix the locator and leave the screen-reader user with an unnamed button.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep the scan over unnamed buttons but compute the threshold from the viewport width (e.g. right half of window.innerWidth) instead of a fixed 850.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Still geometry. It moves the number that has to be re-tuned when the toolbar reflows, leaves the button unnamed for assistive tech, and keeps the fragile loop that produces the misleading downstream failure.

alternatives_considered.approach: Leave the button alone and instead locate it by its position within the topbar (last button before the report-name button, or nth-of-type).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: DOM order is layout too. Adding or reordering a topbar control silently breaks it, and it still leaves a screen reader with nothing to announce.

alternatives_considered.approach: Give the non-compact FiltersButton the name 'Filters' too and drop `exact: true` from the locator.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Contradicts IAC-2 — the locator would then depend on which variant is on the page, and matching 'Filters' loosely is one substring change away from matching the tooltip text as well.

assumptions: packages/desktop-client/locale is gitignored (confirmed via .gitignore:29 and packages/desktop-client/.gitignore:35) and regenerated by `yarn generate:i18n`, so adding a `t('Filters')` call requires no committed locale change — and 'Filters' already exists as a key at FiltersMenu.tsx:744.
The e2e suite runs in English, so getByRole name 'Filters' matches the rendered locale; this matches every other name-based locator already in the suite ('Show Legend', 'Unselect All', 'Category').
Playwright's getByRole name option matches a substring by default and whole-string with exact: true, so `exact: true` is what keeps the locator off the non-compact 'Filter' button.
unknowns: Whether the report topbar overflows rather than reflows below ~1024px. If the toolbar has a min-width that pushes the filter button off-screen entirely, the new e2e case would need the width adjusted; the button is still findable either way, and 1024px was chosen because it is below the 1280px default where x>850 previously held.

Whether the 'Filters' tooltip text is currently exposed to Playwright's accessible-name computation (react-aria renders it in a tooltip element referenced by aria-describedby, and the suite hides [role="tooltip"] via addStyleTag). Adding aria-label makes the question moot — an explicit aria-label always wins — but if a future change removes it, the locator must not silently start matching the tooltip.
residual_risks: Nothing runs reports.test.ts in CI, so a future change that removes the aria-label would be caught by the unit test but not by the e2e suite until someone runs Playwright locally. Stated in the PR body rather than left to be discovered.
The narrow-viewport e2e case proves the locator works at 1024px. It does not prove the topbar is usable at every width; a genuinely broken layout at some other width would still be a separate bug.
